VA-2025-VHA-0073 (September 2, 2025) 
 
Filed via electronic comment portal at Regulations.gov 
 
INTRODUCTION 
My name is William Wagner and I hold the academic rank of Distinguished 
Professor Emeritus (Law). I served on the faculty at the University of Florida and 
Western Michigan University Cooley Law School, where I taught Constitutional Law 
and Ethics. I currently hold the Faith and Freedom Center Distinguished Chair at 
Spring Arbor University. Before joining academia, I served as a federal judge in the 
United States Courts, as Senior Assistant United States Attorney in the Department of 
Justice, and as a Legal Counsel in the United States Senate. I am also the Founding 
President of Salt & Light Global. 
My name is Katherine Bussard and I serve as Executive Director & C.O.O. of 
Salt & Light Global, a faith-based non-profit dedicated to protecting freedom of 
religion, promoting the sanctity of all human life, preserving the family, and 
upholding good governance.  Before joining Salt & Light Global in this capacity, I 
served in local elected office for more than a decade and have severed as board 
member and officer with several charitable community organizations dedicated to 
meeting the needs of the most vulnerable, including women and children.  Finally, I 
am proud to be the wife of a soldier. 
 
Together, we respectfully submit the following Comments on the Notice of 
Proposed Rulemaking, “Reproductive Health Services,” as published by the 
Department of Veteran Affairs (VA) and Veterans Health Administration (VHA); 
RIN: 2900-AS31(P). We fully support this proposal to reinstate the historic 
exclusions on abortion and abortion counseling from the medical benefits package 

for service personnel and veterans and for those eligible for coverage under Civilian 
Health and Medical Program of the Department of Veteran Affairs (CHAMPVA), 
because we believe this course of action to be in the best interest of our nation’s 
heroes and their families, and as a matter of good governance, economic 
stewardship, and human compassion.  
 
PROTECTING THE BEST INTEREST OF OUR NATION’S HEROES & THEIR FAMILIES 
    The US Supreme Court has correctly recognized that government holds a 
“legitimate and substantial interest in preserving and promoting fetal life” and 
women’s health.1  Indeed, there is no government interest greater than the protection of 
human life.  And there is no human life more in need of government protection than a 
defenseless, pre-born child.  In every other sector of society, pre-born children are 
currently protected from the use of federal tax-payer funds to terminate their lives—but 
children living in the wombs of military service personnel or CHAMPVA-eligible 
individuals do not have that same protection. Likewise, military affiliated women 
currently eligible for taxpayer-funded abortion are not protected from the medical and 
substantial mental health risks associated with abortion.2 Military families face unique 
challenges that 99% of the American population cannot relate to: deployments, life-
threating on-the-job hazards, long periods of separation, frequent relocation, and more. 
For spouses coming and going from active service, learning that a spouse had an 
abortion while the other parent was away on military orders can place a unique 
psychological burden on that soldier. Rather than funding and promoting abortion in 
 
1 See, e.g., Gonzales v. Carhart (Carhart II), 550 U.S. 124, 145 (2007); Planned Parenthood v. Casey, 505 U.S. 833, 
871 (1992) (recognizing that a state’s interests in protecting “the potentiality” of human life and the health of 
pregnant women were both important and legitimate).  
2 Medical risks to the physical well-being of women who undergo elective abortions can include bleeding, 
infection, uterine scaring, sepsis, increased risk of breast cancer, substantial increases in pre-term delivery of 
future pregnancies, infertility, or even death. A more complete list of medical complications is listed here: 
https://www.compasscare.info/health-information/abortion/abortion-risks-and-side-effects/ Perhaps even more 
concerning and common are the mental health effects of abortion, which are especially dangerous for female 
soldiers and women in veteran families, who are already dealing with uncommon levels of psychiatric stress.  A 
2011 international medical study of adult women published on the National Library of Medicine found that, “at 
least one-third of the respondents have experienced psychological side effects. Depression, worrying about not 
being able to conceive again and abnormal eating behaviors were reported as dominant psychological 
consequences of abortion among the respondents. Decreased self-esteem, nightmare, guilt, and regret with 
43.7%, 39.5%, 37.5%, and 33.3% prevalence rates have been placed in the lower status, respectively.” 
(https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC3395931/)These challenges are even more severe among younger 
women, and have been well documented across the nation: Biro FM, Wildey LS, Hillard PJ, Rauh J. Acute and long-
term consequences of adolescents who choose abortions. Pediatr Ann. 1986 Oct;15(10):667-73. doi: 
10.3928/0090-4481-19861001-05. PMID: 3785993. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3785993/ ; Similar recent 
findings are discussed in an interview with Harvard Epidemiology Professor Tyler VanderWeele on recent study; 
https://news.harvard.edu/gazette/story/2023/01/abortion-law-suicide-rate-study-adds-to-raging-debate-but-are-
we-missing-point/ ; Zakus G, Wilday S. Adolescent abortion option. Soc Work Health Care. 1987 Summer;12(4):77-
91. doi: 10.1300/J010v12n04_06. PMID: 3433192. https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3433192/.    

military families, the government should seek to provide additional support to military 
families so that welcoming a new child does not seem so daunting.3 However, the 
policy proposal of re-instating a ban on federal funding of abortion as a military 
medical benefit is a huge first step in the right direction when it comes to protecting the 
interests of pre-born children, the health of the pregnant mother, and the wellbeing of 
the whole military family.  
 
UPHOLDING GOOD GOVERNANCE & THE RULE OF LAW 
Furthermore, this proposed rule makes significant strides towards restoring 
good governance and the rule of law. The “Supplementary Information” on this rule 
rightly asserts that, “As a matter of law, it is without question that VA has the 
authority to bar provision of abortion services through the VA medical benefits 
package to veterans.” The majority opinion in Dobbs v. Jackson Women's Health 
Organization, 142 S. Ct. 2228 (2022)4 made it clear that there is no constitutional right to 
an abortion. Furthermore, abortion coverage was never included in the legislation 
passed by the US Congress, and for decades since the inception of the modern VA 
”medical benefits package”, it has been omitted without harm.5   We agree with the 
Department of Veteran Affairs  that, “the 2022 interim final rule6 was not only 
inappropriate as a matter of fact but also was legally questionable.”  We agree that in 
keeping with Executive Orders 12866, 13563, and 14192, the President is faithfully 
exercising the duties of his office to execute the law consistent Congressional intent, 
and that in restoring the previous standards, he is acting to end a “legally 
questionable” practice and reinstate the rule of law.  
 
EXERCISING WISE ECONOMIC STEWARDSHIP 
The Department of Veteran Affairs provides a thorough review in the 
“Regulatory Impact Analysis for RIN 2900-AS31(P)” of the economic impact of 
funding live birth medical costs instead of abortions, estimating just over one million 
dollars in annualized costs. However, the analysis does not consider the long-term 
benefits to the US government when live births are supported instead of abortion. Each

our staff can be of any assistance.

6 See 87 FR 55288 (September 9, 2022). 

new citizen born will pay an average of $524,625 in state and federal taxes, with 
roughly half of that sum funding the US Federal government.7 The Regulatory Impact 
Analysis estimates an increase of about 100 more live births a year as a result of this 
rulemaking, and the lifelong tax revenue of just 5 of those children who grow up and 
contribute our economy will more than offset the projected annualized costs. In fact, 
when one estimates the long-term gains, each year this rulemaking prevails, after 
accounting for annualized costs, the US government stands to add about 23.75 million 
dollars to its coffers. This sum does not consider the monetary benefit to the greater 
national economy of a growing workforce, a growing consumer base, increased 
economic productivity and output, or other economic benefits. However, the bottom 
line is clear: Policy that promotes life promotes economic growth. This rulemaking 
exercises sound economic stewardship.  
 
ACTING WITH HUMAN COMPASSION TOWARDS THE MOST VULNERABLE 
This rulemaking exercises sound ethical policy and acts with human compassion 
towards the most vulnerable. Those 100 pre-born children each year who take up 
residence inside the womb of a solider or CHAMPVA eligible woman have inherent 
human dignity and worth.  Their great value to this nation extends far beyond their 
economic impact and cannot be so simply calculated. They are the children of our 
nation’s heroes and there is no telling what great deeds they will do in and for this 
nation if they are given the opportunity to live outside the womb. As Professor Francis 
Beckwith cogently explains: 
Only artifacts, such as clocks and spaceships, come into existence part by 
part.  Living beings come into existence all at once and then gradually 
unfold to themselves and to the world what they already are, but only 
incipiently are.  Because one can only develop certain functions by 
nature (i.e., a result of basic, intrinsic capacities) a human being at every 
stage of development is never a potential person, she is always a person 
with potential even if that potential is never actualized due to premature 
death or the result of the absence or deformity of a physical state 
necessary to actualize that potential.8  
 
These children are more than just potential life—and government must not continue to 
make the grave mistake of undervaluing their potential or worth. Basic human dignity 
 
7 “A Life of Tax: How Much Tax Will Americans Pay Over Their Lifetime?” https://www.self.inc/info/life-of-
tax/?utm_source=chatgpt.com  
8 Francis J. Beckwith, Defending Life: A Moral and Legal Case Against Abortion Choice (2007) at 34 
(emphasis in original; internal citation omitted). 

and compassion demands that civil government defend the defenseless. Likewise, 
encouraging women—whether soldiers or dependents of soldiers—to experience the 
joy and wonder of motherhood and giving life instead of the trauma and risk of ending 
it—is the most compassionate response for the women involved. Even women in crisis 
and the most traumatic of circumstances deserve to know the truth—that ending 
another human life will not end their crisis.  By providing wraparound services that 
support both the mother and child, the Department can help even the most vulnerable 
find an end to their crisis and break free of trauma.  This is real compassion.   Women 
may still make other choices using other streams of funding, but they are not entitled to 
have the taxpayers of this nation involuntarily fund the destruction of the innocent life 
in their womb.  This proposed rulemaking meets families with honor and compassion 
rather than guilt and shame, and as such, out to be adopted.  
 
CONCLUSION 
Government has a duty to protect the most vulnerable, to wisely steward public 
funds, to uphold good governance, and most of all, to act in the best interest or our 
nation’s heroes and their families.  The Proposed Rulemaking, “Reproductive Health 
Services,” RIN: 2900-AS31, accomplishes all these goals and restores a right standard to 
the Department of Veteran Affairs. We heartily urge its adoption and thank you for 
your thoughtful consideration on this important matter.  
 
 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
//s William Wagner 
WFFC Distinguished Chair for Faith & Freedom, Spring Arbor University 
Distinguished Professor Emeritus (Constitutional Law) 
 
Katherine Bussard 
C.O.O. of Salt & Light Global
